title: Onramp Cookbook: Lightweight Integrations Pilot
body:
Purpose

This is a lightweight, opinionated onramp cookbook for a small pilot we can hand to partner teams and early customers. Goal: get an engineer from 'nothing' to a validated end-to-end integration (dev -> staging -> smoke prod) in ~60 minutes with clear guardrails for cost, latency, and observability.

Audience
- Backend engineers integrating text generation APIs into web services
- Mobile engineers linking embeddings for local search use-cases
- Data scientists validating model outputs in a controlled pipeline

Scope and constraints
- Keep the surface area small: one Node example (API route), one Python worker (embeddings + vector store), one tiny React sample (client-side UX with server proxy).
- No private deployment config in this pilot (hosted API only).
- Provide toggles for: streaming vs non-streaming, synchronous vs async, small/medium model versions.

Success metrics (pilot)
- Time-to-first-success: < 60 minutes for 75% of test users (measured via lab sessions).
- Average token cost observed in smoke run < $0.12 per interaction (bench target).
- Error rate < 1% on smoke traffic; clear fallback behavior for common errors.
- Telemetry: each sample app emits the minimal event set (see telemetry section) and is automatically visible in Console dashboards.

High-level quickstart flow (10–60 minute tiers)
1) 10-minute smoke: create API key, run docker-compose dev that spins a tiny HTTP proxy and sample app, call /generate with example prompt, see streaming response in browser.
2) 30-minute validation: swap model to medium, run 100 synthetic requests locally, observe latency P50/P95, verify cost estimate and warnings for high token usage.
3) 60-minute end-to-end: wire embedding pipeline, index 100 doc snippets into the vector store, perform similarity search -> generate answer, run basic eval (precision@k) script.

Assets to include in repo
- preseeded .env.example with placeholders: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_URL, REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID
- docker-compose.dev.yml: node+python containers, local sqlite vectorstore for speed
- /samples/node-express/generate.ts (minimal 25-line example using Redwood SDK streaming API)
- /samples/python/embeddings_worker.py (batch upload + retrieval example)
- /samples/react/client.tsx (simple chat/stream consumer with optimistic UI)
- README.md with the 3-tier checklist (10/30/60) and one-command flows: "make smoke" -> runs dev compose, "make bench" -> synthetic traffic job

Developer experience details (opinionated)
- Default to streaming on sample Node route; show non-streaming variant as a comment in the code.
- Include a small local proxy that injects per-request metadata header (x-rw-dev-phase: pilot) to ensure Console can filter pilot traffic.
- Suggest model pinning in sample .yaml: model: redwood/medium:v1.1 and a fallback: redwood/small:v1.
- Provide a toggle for intelligent batching: env var RW_ENABLE_BATCHING=true that starts an in-process batcher in python worker for embeddings ingestion.

Telemetry contract (minimal events)
- event: integration.started (tags: sample-name, user-email if present)
- event: request.sent (tags: model, tokens_in, tokens_out, streaming:boolean)
- event: response.latency (ms)
- event: fallback.invoked (reason)
- event: eval.run (baseline_id, pass_rate)
Make sure examples show how to emit these to Console (SDK snippet + curl example).

Safety and cost guardrails
- Recommend server-side token cap per-request: MAX_TOKENS=1024 default in .env.example
- Provide a middleware snippet that rejects requests with estimated cost > $0.50 (pre-flight estimation via token heuristic).
- Document automatic fallback policy: if P95 latency > 2s on the chosen model, automatically reroute to fallback small model and emit fallback.invoked.

Docs outline (what to write in README + short cheat sheets)
- Quickstart: 5 commands to go from checkout -> smoke test (with expected outputs)
- API reference: minimal table of SDK methods used in samples (generate, stream, embeddings.upsert, embeddings.query)
- Troubleshooting: common errors and one-line fixes (401 -> check REDWOOD_API_KEY, 429 -> backoff example, streaming partial frames -> connection keepalive note)
- FAQ: why streaming? why pin models? when to enable batching?

Microcopy and UX copy suggestions (for sample apps)
- Streaming placeholder: "Assistant is typing..." -> show token-level progress spinner with small toast "Cost est: $0.01"
- Error toast: "We hit a hiccup — retrying with a smaller model to keep things snappy."
- Onboarding modal: short bullets: "1) Create API key 2) Run make smoke 3) Try the example prompt"

Developer testing and gating
- Add a lightweight end-to-end test that runs in CI job "devx/pilot-smoke": starts the containers, runs 5 sample requests, asserts 200 + non-empty text + < 2s median latency (on GitHub actions runner baseline).
- Create an integration checklist PR template for partner teams (confirm telemetry, cost estimate, fallback policy implemented).

Open questions / risks
- Do we want sample repos to call the hosted Console ingestion API directly, or to emit events via a stubbed local collector? (Tradeoff: Console visibility vs friction for partners.)
- Embedding indexing storage: sqlite is fastest for lab but might give bad signal about real-world cold starts on vector DBs. Mitigation: include a short note on expected differences and a tiny script to spike on a cloud vector DB (optional).
- CI baseline latency: GH Actions runners vary — need to mark timing assertions as soft thresholds and gate on correctness first.

Action items (next week)
- [Maya] scaffold repo layout and Docker compose (ETA 3 working days)
- [Liam] write Node streaming sample and minimal README quickstart (ETA 2 days)
- [Aisha] python embeddings worker + batching toggle + telemetry hooks (ETA 4 days)
- [Ethan] CI smoke job + PR template and Confluence stub (ETA 5 days)
- Schedule 1-hour lab with 6 engineers to validate 10/30/60 timings (target: 2025-01-22)

Notes to self
- Keep copy short — the README should be a single page with bolded 3-step path to success.
- Avoid too many knobs; expose only 2 env toggles for the pilot: RW_ENABLE_BATCHING and RW_ENABLE_STREAMING.
- Add a short script to estimate cost for a run: python tools/estimate_cost.py --model redwood/medium --tokens 350

References and inspiration
- Internal: /shared_drives/product/hosted-api/quickstart-reference (use metrics table as benchmark)
- External: minimal examples from open-source inference repos, but keep attribution in README

-- end of doc --
